construct: a link whose focus ring is spelled ONLY as a KEYWORD flip — the rest plane carries `outline-width: 3px; outline-style: none` with no `outline-color` of its own (so it computes to `currentColor`), and `:focus-visible` sets `outline-style: solid; outline-width: 2px; outline-offset: 2px` and nothing else
why: THIS IS altitude.link's EXACT SHAPE, and the row RC3 could not close. `outline-style` is the keyword that decides whether CSS paints a ring at all, so a library that flips only the keyword hands the state plane a WIDTH delta and no colour delta. core/emit-figma-script.ts's translateStateOverrides asks for the pair inside the OVERRIDE — `outline-color !== undefined && outline-width !== undefined` — so the ring never lowers and the focus-visible preview is byte-identical to the base cell. Every fact needed is already measured and carried: the keyword in declaredStates, the width in states, and the hue as the part's own `color` (the currentColor fold that detectFolds records by name). The previous round wrote this down as a wall on the premise that completing the pair 'would mean inventing a hue'; the hue is not invented, it is CSS's own initial value for outline-color and the very ink the generated CSS surface paints the ring with.
